podcast.title: Pre-Sloan Roots Rock Ensemble
podcast.body: Blackpool was a pre-Sloan "Roots Rock band" in which Chris Murphy played bass. He joined primarily to record with renowned producer Terry Brown, who was holding open recording sessions. The band practiced equal money splitting, a tradition later adopted by Sloan. "It was more kind of a Roots Rock band, but at the time I was still into hardcore basically."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Sloan In Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.title: Renowned Producer and Studio Mentor
podcast.body: Terry Brown is a notable producer known for working on "some of their [Rush's] biggest records." He was also present during the recording of The Who's "Substitute" and The Trogs' "Wild Thing." During a session with Blackpool, he strictly instructed Chris Murphy to play only root notes on the bass, a technique Murphy jokingly still refers to as "footballs." "Terry Brown, a guy who worked with Russian, some of their biggest records, ended up working with them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
